Title Tag

You might say

Give every product detail page a tab title containing its product name, while keeping the H1 in the page.

The HTML title that identifies the current document·The browser uses it in a tab or window title, and a search system may use it when generating a result title. It should distinguish the current page, but the page H1 and a search result title are not the same field.
Know first
HTML
HTML title
Who sees the page title
product.html
1<head>
2<title>Noise-cancelling headphones · Pine Store</title>
3</head>
4<h1>Noise-cancelling headphones</h1>
→
Browser tabNoise-cancelling headphones · Pine Store
Search title candidateNoise-cancelling headphones · Pine Storepine.example/products/headphones

The H1 and document title can be related, but they are separate objects to verify.

How the title and page content divide the job

It first serves the browser tab: The title lives in the document head and identifies the current document in the browser. A detail page should include a name that distinguishes the object rather than reuse one generic title everywhere.

Search results are not a fixed echo: A search system may use the title, page text, or other signals to generate a result title. Verify the browser tab and source metadata; do not treat exact search echoing as guaranteed.

It is not the H1 or search title

Title Tag is the document title in the head; an H1 in HTML is a content heading; a search system may use either but can rewrite its result title. Changing the H1 does not automatically change the title element.

Give each product detail page a distinct title that includes the product name, while keeping the page H1. Switch between two products and verify that the browser tab changes; do not promise that search results will copy the title exactly.
